amendments.why: Three verse passes in this chapter cited rule 22's first sentence to leave the enclitic demonstrative of 'ey-zeh unrepresented beside a rendered interrogative, against unanimous corpus precedent (six units fuse the compound, none splits it). The correction belongs in the rule the passes actually reached for, and rule 22 already carries the paragraph that distinguishes an element the ASV left unwritten from one it wrote inside a fused word; the new group extends that paragraph to a compound whose second morpheme resumes nothing. It is kept lemma-specific on purpose: the corpus leaves the deictic of lammah-zeh and ben-mi-zeh unrepresented in sixteen units, so a general rule about semantically bleached enclitics would contradict it, and the boundary is stated in the rule so a later reader does not widen it. Nothing else in rule 22 is altered.
amendments.rule: A repeated or resumptive element that the ASV renders once is still its own unit. Mark the unrepresented occurrence `unrepresented` rather than folding it into the rendered one. Where the repetition is a counted noun distributed across a compound numeral — Hebrew writes one `שָׁנָה` per numeral group where the ASV writes a single *years* — the rendered occurrence is the last, closing the whole Hebrew figure as the English noun closes the whole English one. Do not settle it by number agreement: Hebrew writes `שָׁנִים` after 2–10 and `שָׁנָה` from 11 up whatever the total, while the English plural follows the sum, so a match between them is an accident of two unrelated agreement systems and is not evidence. Do not settle it by which numeral the English noun stands beside either, since English drives the counted noun to the end of the phrase whatever order the translation chose. Tail-to-tail is what survives, and it holds across both Hebrew group orders and the ASV's frequent reordering of them. The genealogies are where this recurs, and BSB, which attaches the noun to its own phrase, disagrees on every first occurrence. **Tail-to-tail governs a run of absolute occurrences only.** Where the phrase is instead headed by a **construct** — a regnal date such as `בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע שָׁנָה` → *In the twenty and seventh year* — the construct is what the English realizes, and the trailing absolute is the resumptive occurrence that goes `unrepresented`. So the rendered occurrence is the last of several absolutes but the first where a construct heads them, and MACULA's morphology is what decides which case this is. Position is the consequence, not the rule. **But a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a fused English word is not an unrendered occurrence.** Where a relative clause resumes its antecedent with a pronominal suffix on a preposition, or with a resumptive adverb, and the ASV writes one pronominal adverb for the whole — *wherein*, *whereon*, *whereby*, *whither*, and the bare *therein* of a preposition and its own suffix — the relative, the preposition and the resumptive morpheme share one unit under rule 30, headed on the relative, or on the preposition where no relative stands. Do not mark the suffix `unrepresented` under this rule's first sentence: rule 30's one-English-word condition is met, because that word carries the resumption as well as the relation, exactly as *Nor* carries both the coordination and the negation in rule 35. The corpus reads `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ` → *wherein* as one three-morpheme unit in twenty-one places and `בָּהּ` → *therein* as one two-morpheme unit in sixty-one, and records no unit where such a suffix stands outside the word. So ask first whether the English word carries the morpheme's sense: what this rule's first sentence governs is an element the ASV has left unwritten, as a second `בֵּין` or a surplus `שָׁנָה` is, and not one it has written inside a fusion. **The interrogative `אֵי` with a following `זֶה` is one interrogative expression, and its demonstrative is not an unrendered occurrence either.** Where the ASV renders `אֵי־זֶה` by a single interrogative word — *where*, *what*, *which* — the two morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on `אֵי`, which carries the wh-lexeme; the demonstrative is enclitic to the compound rather than a repeated or resumptive element, so this rule's first sentence does not reach it and it is never marked `unrepresented` beside a rendered `אֵי`. A construction-supplied copula joining that unit does not defeat rule 30's one-rendering condition, exactly as it does not for `לִפְנֵי` → *was before*, so `אֵי־זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ` → ***Where is*** *the way* fuses as `אֵי־זֶה` → *what* does. The corpus fuses this compound in every unit it records — JER.6.16, 1KI.13.12, ISA.66.1 twice, ECC.11.6 and 1KI.22.24 — and splits it in none. Two limits. Where the ASV spends a word on each morpheme, the condition is unmet and rule 2 splits them as usual. And this governs `אֵי־זֶה` and no other pair: a deictic `זֶה` standing after an interrogative that keeps its own English word — the `זֶה` of `לָמָּה זֶּה` or of `בֶּן־מִי־זֶה`, and the `זֶה` of `מִי זֶה` where the ASV writes *this* for it — is this rule's ordinary case, rendered where the ASV writes a word for it and `unrepresented` where it does not. **A resumptive possessive suffix is read on exactly those terms, and it need not stand on a preposition.** Where the clause resumes its antecedent with a suffix on a noun inside it and the ASV writes one *whose* for the pair, the relative and that suffix share one unit under rule 30, headed on the relative, while the noun keeps its own English: `אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אֲבָנֶיהָ בַרְזֶל` → *a land* ***whose*** *stones are iron* is one unit on `אֲשֶׁר` and the suffix, with *stones* left to `אֶבֶן`. Contiguity is not the condition, for the reason rule 35 gives: however much of the clause stands between them, the one English word still carries both the relation and the resumption, so nothing is left over to mark. The corpus reads `אֲשֶׁר` with its resumptive suffix as one *whose* unit at DEU.28.49 and 1KI.8.39, and as a `noncompositional` one at AMO.2.9 and DAN.10.1 among eighteen such places. **But read which morphemes stand in each clause before counting a second occurrence.** Where a further clause is coordinated under the one written relative and the ASV rewrites its *whose* at the head of that clause, a resumptive suffix standing in that clause is what the second word realizes, under rule 18's sentence giving a suffix the English relative pronoun that renders it: `וּמֵהֲרָרֶיהָ תַּחְצֹב נְחֹשֶׁת` → *and out of* ***whose*** *hills thou mayest dig copper* gives its *whose* to the suffix on `הֲרָרֶיהָ`, not to the relative as a repetition under rule 25. Where no such suffix stands in the coordinated clause, rule 55's distributed subordinator governs as before and every occurrence is the relative's. **And read whether the suffix points at the antecedent at all before treating it as resumptive.** Every fusion above rests on a morpheme that resumes the antecedent, and a pronominal suffix standing inside the relative clause does that only where its referent is the antecedent; agreement is the first check and reference decides, so read MACULA's person, gender and number against the noun the clause modifies. Where the suffix instead denotes something else the clause speaks of, the one English pronominal adverb carries the relative's own relation and nothing of that suffix, rule 30's condition is unmet for it, and the fusion does not reach it: the relative takes the adverb alone, the suffix takes whatever English pronoun the ASV writes for it under rule 18, and the preposition it stands on is disposed of by rules 11 and 40 like any other. `וְאֶת־תַּחֲלֻאֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר־חִלָּה יְהוָה בָּהּ` → *and the sicknesses* ***wherewith*** *Jehovah hath made* ***it*** *sick* gives *wherewith* to `אֲשֶׁר` alone, *it* to the suffix of `בָּהּ`, which is feminine singular and denotes the land rather than the masculine plural `תַּחֲלֻאִים` the relative modifies, and leaves the `בְּ` `unrepresented` under rule 40, since the ASV promotes its object to the direct object of *made ... sick*. A relative left holding such a word by itself is not a unit short of its parts: the corpus aligns a bare `אֲשֶׁר` to *wherewith* in fifty-five units, and its *wherein* units include bare relatives beside the three-morpheme fusions. Count the English pronouns against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s: where the ASV writes a pronoun besides the adverb, some morpheme other than the relative answers for it, and where it writes none, the resumption is inside the adverb and the paragraphs above govern.

conventions: The interrogative compound 'ey-zeh is aligned as one fused unit under rule 30 wherever the ASV renders it by a single interrogative word, headed on 'ey, which carries the wh-lexeme; the enclitic demonstrative is never marked unrepresented beside it, and a construction-supplied copula joining the unit (Where is, 38.19 twice) does not defeat rule 30's one-rendering condition. This is not the mi zeh of 38.2, where the ASV writes this for the demonstrative, each morpheme owns a word, and rule 2 splits the pair. The corpus fuses 'ey-zeh in all six units it records (JER.6.16, 1KI.13.12, ISA.66.1 twice, ECC.11.6, 1KI.22.24) and splits it in none, while it leaves the deictic of lammah-zeh and ben-mi-zeh unrepresented in sixteen; read which compound is written before choosing.

report: Read all 43 candidate groups and then the dump end to end for the added units the table cannot see. Every group but one is the ASV rendering one word differently in contexts the source licenses: waw connectives read off the ASV (and / or / but / then / that); the interrogative particle taking a written auxiliary in 38.12, 16, 17, 22, 31, 32, 34, 35 and 39, going unrepresented where the question is marked by inversion alone (38.33) and where the existential holds the possessive verb (38.28); an article taking a written 'the' or going unrepresented where the ASV writes 'a' (38.38) or nothing (38.24, 38.30); and the prepositions following the ASV's recastings. None of those is a split.

One real finding, and it is a split against the corpus rather than within the chapter: the fixed interrogative 'ey-zeh' at 38.19 (twice) and 38.24 was aligned on 'ey alone, with the enclitic demonstrative marked unrepresented under rule 22. The corpus fuses 'ey-zeh under rule 30 in every unit it records - 'where is' (JER.6.16), 'what' (1KI.13.12, ISA.66.1), 'which' (ECC.11.6), 'what manner of' (ISA.66.1), 'which way' (1KI.22.24) - and splits it in none; JER.6.16's own note weighs and rejects the reading this chapter took. Both verses are patched: one unit per compound, headed on 'ey, with the construction-supplied copula joining it in 38.19 as rule 30 allows.

The patch is scoped to 'ey + zeh and touches nothing else. 'mi zeh' at 38.2 is deliberately left split, because the ASV writes 'this' for the demonstrative there, so each morpheme owns a word and rule 2 governs; the corpus agrees, leaving a lammah-zeh or ben-mi-zeh deictic unrepresented in 16 units and rendering it in 7.

BSB: three of the eleven disagreements (the demonstratives of 38.19 twice and 38.24) resolve as a consequence of the patch, but they are corroboration and not the ground for it (rule 38). The other eight are documented convention differences and none is an error - the object marker at 38.1 (rule 16); 'el at 38.22 and be- at 38.11, silenced by recastings the ASV writes without a preposition (rule 40); the interrogative particle and the possessive le- at 38.28, where rule 43's closing paragraph keeps 'Hath' on the existential and leaves both unrepresented; the interrogative particle at 38.33, a question marked by inversion (rule 17); the article at 38.24, for which the ASV writes no 'the' (rule 29); and the object suffix at 38.32, resumed once in 'the Bear with her train' (rule 22).

Considered and left as defensible, each with its competing reading already in the verse's own notes: the added 'its' at 38.18, where rule 25's resumed-referent paragraph would give the possessive to 'erets against rule 18's closing sentence; the added 'ground' at 38.27, which completes both coordinated nominals equally; and the two separate added units at 38.30. Changing these would be churn, not correction.

One convention recorded (the treatment of 'ey-zeh against the split demonstrative of mi zeh) and one amendment to rule 22, whose first sentence is what drew three verse passes into the error. The amendment is deliberately lemma-specific: the corpus splits the deictic of lammah-zeh and ben-mi-zeh in sixteen units, so a general rule about bleached enclitics would contradict it.
